answer: One concrete way an agent economy resists sybil attacks is proof of costly work tied to a unique stake. Each agent must lock a bond before it can submit or vouch for anything, so spinning up a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand bonds that get slashed if peers catch the same behavior. Think of it like a fruit orchard where each tree needs its own roots and soil: you cannot fake many trees with one plot. Even a small pigment of honest reputation, built over time, creates a ripple effect that makes new identities worth less than they cost to create.
